Diagnosis done. Your Hyprland config is **not** the problem — it's applied correctly at runtime (verified: `gaps_in=0`, animations off, Framework keyboard on `colemak`).

## Root cause: your systemd **user manager** has `HOME=/`

```
$ systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath
UnitPath=/.config/systemd/user      ← should be /home/sauyon/.config/systemd/user
$ systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME
HOME=/
```

So systemd searches `/.config/systemd/user` and **cannot see a single home-manager user unit**, even though all ~30 symlinks exist in `~/.config/systemd/user/`:

```
$ systemctl --user status waybar
Unit waybar.service could not be found.
```

Both your symptoms are the same bug:

| Symptom | Dead unit |
|---|---|
| No waybar | `waybar.service` (you have `systemd.enable = true`) |
| Monitors wrong | `kanshi.service` — the `Modular` profile (Dell P3424WEB at `-528,-1440`, laptop at `0,0`) never applies, so Hyprland falls back to its catch-all `position = "auto"` → eDP-1 at `0x0`, DP-5 at `2560x0`, side by side |

Also dead for the same reason: `hypridle`, `hyprpaper`, `walker`, `ssh-tpm-agent`, `sops-nix`, the xdg portals.

**Why `HOME=/`:** `sauyon` is a systemd-homed LUKS user (`/home/sauyon.home`, uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`). The manager (pid 2107) started `Jul 30 21:52:32`, 2m14s after boot, triggered by a `Service=remote` session — before the encrypted home was resolvable. UnitPath is computed once at manager start, so it's been wrong for this entire 17-hour boot.

---
name: project_tailscale_ssh_poisons_user_manager
description: On utsuho, an early Tailscale SSH login starts systemd --user with HOME=/ before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot
metadata:
  type: project
---

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), an inbound **Tailscale SSH** connection that lands before
Sauyon logs in physically permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. Tailscale SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>`
   → PAM service **`remote`** (`Service=remote` in `loginctl show-session`).
2. `login -f` **skips the PAM auth stack**, so `pam_systemd_home.so` (auth, `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6`)
   never runs → the LUKS home is never unlocked.
3. `pam_systemd.so` (session, `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20`) still runs → logind creates
   the session → starts `user@60006.service`.
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `systemd --user` gets **`HOME=/`** → its unit search
   path becomes `/.config/systemd/user`. UnitPath is computed **once at manager start**,
   so it stays poisoned for the entire boot even after the home later unlocks.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**This is a Tailscale SSH interaction bug, not a systemd bug** — systemd's `HOME=/`
fallback and start-time UnitPath are by design.

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Workaround (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.

You're right — `HOME=/` is explicit homed configuration, and my "systemd falls back when the home is unusable" framing was wrong.

## What's actually happening

`docs/USER_RECORD.md` documents `useFallback`: when a login can't release the disk encryption key, homed flips `useFallback: true` and `fallbackHomeDirectory`/`fallbackShell` **override** the real ones. Your record has `fallbackHomeDirectory: "/"` literally. The stated purpose is to let "subsystems such as SSH" log into an account whose home needs further unlocking.

And it's definitely not a generic missing-home fallback — I tested: systemd sets `HOME=/usr/share/empty` for user `passim`, a directory that doesn't exist.

## Where the real defect is

`useFallback` is scoped to a **login session**. But that same login starts `user@60006.service`, which is **boot-scoped** — so a deliberately-degraded per-login value gets baked into a long-lived service and is never re-evaluated when `useFallback` flips back to `false`. That's a known open upstream bug: [systemd#30727](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/30727) (labels `homed` + `pid1`, still open) and [#36769](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/36769) (closed as dup of #34151).

## So is my drop-in wrong?

It's a workaround against an intentional mechanism, which I should have said. Two things make it narrower than it looks:

1. `Environment=` on `user@60006.service` only sets the **manager's** env. A locked SSH login still gets `fallbackShell` (`/usr/bin/systemd-home-fallback-shell` → `homectl`) from its own session lookup and can still unlock — the fallback UX is intact.
2. While locked, `/home/sauyon` doesn't exist and `/home` is root-owned `0755`, so nothing can write into a path that later gets shadowed. Pinning HOME degrades to the same "writes fail" as `/`.

Memory corrected. But it's your call whether to keep an override of a deliberate mechanism.

# Watch for sauyon's systemd-homed LUKS home to become available.
#
# Companion to user@60006.service.d/10-home.conf. That drop-in guarantees the user
# manager's unit search path is /home/sauyon/.config/systemd/user even when the manager
# is started by a passwordless login (Tailscale SSH, etc.) before the home is unlocked.
# But at that moment the directory does not exist yet, so the first scan finds nothing.
#
# This path unit fires the instant the directory appears -- i.e. whenever the home is
# unlocked, by ANY route: Tailscale SSH landing in homed's fallbackShell and typing the
# password, a physical login, or a manual `homectl activate`. The service it triggers
# makes the already-running user manager rescan, so every home-manager unit comes up
# without a logout and without Tailscale having to change anything.
#
# systemd watches the deepest existing ancestor and walks down as components appear, so
# a fully absent /home/sauyon is fine. Re-arms automatically if the home is deactivated.

Description=Watch for sauyon's homed home to be mounted

[Path]
PathExists=/home/sauyon/.config/systemd/user
Unit=sauyon-user-units-rescan.service

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
